title: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
statement: A room has `n` seats and `n` students, all on a number line: `seats[i]` is where seat `i` is and `students[j]` is where student `j` stands. Several seats, or several students, may share a position. In one move, a single student steps one unit left or right. Every student must end up on a seat, with no seat holding two students. Return the smallest total number of moves that achieves this.
notes:
## Intuition

Each student pays the distance to the seat they take, so the task is to pair students with seats to minimise the total distance. Trying every pairing is n! work. The key fact: if two pairs cross (a left student takes a right seat while a right student takes a left seat), swapping their seats never costs more. Removing every crossing leaves the sorted pairing: the k-th smallest student takes the k-th smallest seat.

## Approach

1. Sort `seats` ascending.
2. Sort `students` ascending.
3. Walk both arrays with the same index `i` and add `Math.abs(seats[i] - students[i])` to `moves`.
4. Return `moves`.

## Example 1, step by step

`seats = [3, 1, 5]` sorts to `[1, 3, 5]`; `students = [2, 7, 4]` sorts to `[2, 4, 7]`.

| i | seat | student | distance | moves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 3 | 4 | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 5 | 7 | 2 | 4 |

The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the two sorts; the scan is O(n). (With positions at most 100, a counting sort would make it linear.)
- Space: O(1) beyond the in-place sorts.

## Pitfalls

- Sort numerically with `(a, b) => a - b`; JavaScript's default sort compares as strings, so `10` would come before `9`.
- Use the absolute difference: a student may need to move left or right.
- Matching each student to their nearest free seat greedily in input order is not optimal; only the sorted pairing is guaranteed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seats`, `students` | the positions, sorted ascending in place |
| `i` | index of the current pair (the i-th smallest of each) |
| `moves` | total distance walked so far |

narration.2: Sort the seats so the smallest seat comes first.
narration.3: Sort the students the same way so equal ranks line up.
narration.6: Pair the i-th smallest student with the i-th smallest seat.
narration.7: That student walks the distance between the two positions.
narration.9: The sorted pairing has no crossings, so this total is the minimum.
